key_insight: The paper stabilizes neural constitutive modeling by combining a multi-mode RUDE backbone with conditioning improvements and thermodynamic constraints, yielding interpretable and more reliable rheology predictions.
engineering_relevance: It enables data-driven material models that are safer to train and more trustworthy to deploy in CFD and polymer processing simulations under unseen flow conditions.
method: Log-compress invariants and use a split-network architecture to improve training conditioning.
Apply a differentiable projection layer to enforce the Clausius--Duhem inequality at every time step.
Summarize learned tensor-basis contributions with the compact “rheome” representation for interpretability.
evidence_signal: The framework was tested on synthetic multi-mode Giesekus data and an experimental entangled silicone polymer melt, trained on LAOS, and remained stable and accurate on unseen steady shear, transient stress growth, and extensional flows.
watch_item: The approach adds model and constraint complexity, so implementation must carefully preserve differentiability and numerical stability in large-scale simulation workflows.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
